note.simple: The tower puts your parcel inside a bigger one addressed to the mobile core, so the network can find your phone wherever you walk.
note.technical: The gNB wraps the phone’s own IP packet in IP/UDP/GTP-U (port 2152) to the UPF; the TEID identifies this phone’s session.

ovhl.name: Outer version, IHL
ovhl.about: The outer IPv4 header starts: version 4, 20 bytes.

otos.name: Outer DSCP/ECN
otos.about: Traffic class of the tunnel packet.

olen.name: Outer total length
olen.about: The tunnel packet, with your whole packet inside.

ottl.name: Outer TTL
ottl.about: Counts routers inside the operator’s network; your packet’s own TTL isn’t touched.

odst.about: The other end: the tower on the way down, the core (UPF) on the way up.

usum.name: UDP checksum
usum.about: 0: not used (the inner packet has its own).

flags.name: GTP flags
flags.about: Version 1, GTP (not GTP′), an extension header follows.

length.name: GTP length
length.about: Bytes after the first 8 of the GTP header.

teid.about: Tunnel endpoint ID: which phone’s session this is. Each end picks the TEID it wants to receive.

seqext.name: Sequence, N-PDU, next ext.
seqext.about: Optional fields; 0x85 = a PDU session container follows.

pdu.name: PDU session container
pdu.about: Direction and QoS flow (QFI) of the packet, matching the radio side.

note.simple: The radio controller puts your parcel inside a bigger one addressed to the mobile company’s gate, so the network can find your phone wherever you walk.
note.technical: With Direct Tunnel the RNC wraps the phone’s own IP packet in IP/UDP/GTP-U (port 2152) to the GGSN; the TEID names this phone’s PDP context.

odst.about: The other end: the RNC on the way down, the GGSN on the way up.

teid.about: Tunnel endpoint ID: which phone’s PDP context this is. Each end picks the TEID it wants to receive.

seqext.about: Optional fields; a 3G user packet usually has none, so the header is just 8 bytes (drawn here at today’s size).

pdu.about: 5G’s QoS flow label (5G came in 2019); 3G had none: the PDP context itself carried the QoS.
